Hands-on activity · printable card

Quick card · AI for screening and extraction

View source on GitHubLast updated 6 November 2026

Question: Are hand hygiene interventions effective in reducing healthcare-associated infections? Compare with: the reference review, Pruna et al., J Clin Med 2026 (12 included studies; screening and extraction by two human reviewers without AI; provisional). Screening answers after step 1, extraction answers after step 3. Full guide: activity/README.md (on your own: section "Doing it on your own (self-paced)", 60-90 min)

Work on your own, on your own laptop: you drive the AI, then you verify it. Site: Start page, then one tap per material.

Include only if ALL are met
C1 Acute care hospital (not long-term care, outpatient, rehabilitation, veterinary)
C2 Hospital-wide or more than one ward (not a single ICU, NICU, ED or unit)
C3 Multimodal hand hygiene intervention, clearly central (not one isolated measure; not a broad bundle)
C4 Interrupted time series or before-after (not RCTs, cross-sectional, outbreak reports, reviews)
C5 At least one clinical HAI outcome (not only compliance or hand rub use)
C6 English

Step 1 · Screening · 10 min Copy batch 1 (R001-R020) from the Records page and the screening prompt from the Start page (criteria already in it). Paste both into a new chat. Then paste the AI's answer into the Scorer as it is: no file to save. Coverage line first: "Screened 20 of 60" is expected; fewer means records were dropped. In doubt or no abstract: unsure.

Step 2 · Look at the errors · 10 min (screening answers: now) The Scorer lists the missed includes and the false includes. Open 2 of them (title and abstract, PubMed link) and decide yourself why the AI got them wrong: which criterion, and was it right? Keep one error for the discussion.

Step 3 · Short extraction · 10 min (extraction answers: after this step) Paper Phan2020 (Papers page: Copy full text), the extraction prompt with 5 fields already filled in: country, study_design, intervention_components, primary_hai_outcome, direction_of_effect. Each value with a verbatim quote and its location, or not reported. Verify 2 quotes with Ctrl+F. Compare with the reference values on the Answers page. Read the notes: some papers contradict themselves.

Discussion · 10 min: each person brings one error they found.

Going further: a second run in a new chat; the 11 core fields; the discrepancy log and the AI use record; the agent track (all 60 records, 3 papers, skills, python3 activity/tools/score_screening.py ... --expect-all).

Ask yourself: Performance: would I accept this sensitivity? Transparency: can I trace every value? Bias: whose errors, which studies? Oversight: would I sign the table? Reproducibility: would a second run agree? And the reference: is it always right?

For learning only. These prompts are teaching material for this workshop. They are not a validated method. If you are not confident with how large language models work (context windows, parsing, sampling, retrieval, hallucination) and with advanced techniques (structured outputs, verification against the source, reproducibility checks, documentation of model and version), do not use AI to conduct a real evidence review. You stay responsible for every decision: the AI does not.
